caseStudy.kicker: Case study · iOS · Core ML · Vision
caseStudy.title: AppleDetect
caseStudy.lead: An iOS app that grades apples with on-device machine learning: the camera detects every apple in a crate, a Core ML model sorts each one into quality classes, and the result guides which crate it goes into.

brief.title: The brief
text: Sorting apples by quality is slow by hand. The client wanted a phone to look at a crate and tell which apples belong in which class, without sending images to a server.

contributions.title: What I did
items: Built the native iOS app in Swift with Vision and Core ML.
Integrated a Create ML object-detection model that finds and boxes every apple, with tuned confidence and overlap thresholds.
Used DeepLabV3 segmentation to remove the background.
Added live camera capture and an image cropper.
Built a performance monitor showing CPU, memory, FPS and inference time, and the count of detected apples.

team.title: Team
team.text: I built the iOS app and the machine learning integration myself. The work integrates an existing model; no claim on model training or accuracy.

outcome.title: The result
outcome.text: Apple grading that runs entirely on the device, with live feedback on how fast the model runs.
